title: Keep one-time passwords private
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Do not disclose an OTP to a caller or someone claiming to be bank support. SBI states that it does not ask customers for OTPs.

title: Protect account passwords
source_section: Safety Tips for Passwords, printed page 14
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Keep passwords private and use a different strong password for each account. Enable multi-factor authentication where available.

title: Unsolicited remote-access requests
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Do not install a third-party application at the request of someone claiming to represent SBI. A request to install remote-control software can expose your device and banking information.

title: Verify banking and KYC requests independently
source_section: Financial App KYC Frauds: modus operandi and precautions
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Treat unexpected KYC calls asking you to install remote-access software or disclose card details with caution. Verify the request with the bank through an independently obtained official contact.

title: Check unexpected banking links
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Phishing messages imitate trusted organisations to collect personal or financial information. Check the destination carefully and pause before acting on urgent links asking for sensitive details.

title: Receiving money does not require sharing a UPI PIN
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Do not disclose an OTP or UPI PIN to receive money. If a caller asks for payment credentials, use the institution’s independently verified customer-care channel.

title: Pause when threatened with account closure
source_section: Phishing account deactivation example, printed page 4
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: A message threatening immediate account deactivation may be phishing. Pause before following its verification link and independently check the request with your bank.

title: Verify threats from alleged officials
source_name: I4C / National Cybercrime Threat Analytics Unit
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Do not transfer money under pressure from a caller claiming to be police or another authority. Verify the claim directly with your local police station. Report cyber fraud promptly through cybercrime.gov.in or 1930.

title: Check investment platforms and brokers
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from the named official publication; no user evidence. Publication date is null when not established.
content: Be cautious of trading apps promising high returns with little risk. Check that the broker is SEBI-registered and use the registered broker’s official app or website instead of transferring funds to personal accounts.

title: Beware of paid recovery offers
source_section: How To Avoid Refund and Recovery Scams
provenance_note: Manually paraphrased from official government guidance. US source used only for general recovery-scam precautions; no US reporting or legal advice.
content: Do not pay an unsolicited contact who promises to recover money lost to a scam for an upfront fee. Independently verify organisations that contact you, and do not disclose financial credentials to obtain a refund.
